The video highlights the historical heritage of several businesses, including a popular juice shop in Damascus and a dairy shop in Istanbul. In the first instance, the establishment identifiable by clusters of bananas hanging beneath its signage is Abu Shakir, which was established in 1953 according to the year displayed prominently on its exterior sign. This location is celebrated for its thick smoothies, and the participants are shown consuming a dense avocado and banana blend from large ceramic mugs that have thick gold-rimmed borders and ornate floral patterns on their sides.

The second business featured is Karak6y Muhallebicisi in Istanbul, where the founding year 1943 is etched into the transparent entry glass in reflective lettering. At this venue, the participant is seen spreading kaimak, a rich dairy product made from buffalo milk, onto slices of bread that have been toasted until they are dark brown and crispy. He spreads the dairy substance using a large silver carving fork instead of a knife. The quality of this substance is emphasized as it is paired with tea to form a classic Turkish breakfast.

By comparing these founding dates, it can be determined that the Abu Shakir establishment was founded 10 years after the Karak6y Muhallebicisi shop. While the Damascus business has a legacy dating back to the mid-20th century, the Istanbul dairy specialist predates it by only a decade, representing a much closer historical timeline than previously established.
